Pickens County also claims one 4-year college, Central Wesleyan College, in addition to Clemson University at Clemson which, until 1967, was a part of Oconee County.
Both Oconee and Pickens operate public health programs centered in Walhalla and Pickens, respectively. Pickens County has 2 hospitals, the 98 bed Baptist Hospital and Cannon Memorial Hospital with 75 beds. The Oconee Memorial Hospital currently has 200 beds with an additional 40 planned.
The Sheriff's Department for Oconee County numbers 19 personnel and for Pickens, 25. These forces receive assistance from the South Carolina Highway Patrol as needed.
2.4 CLIMATE AND AIR QUALITY
2.4.1 Climate
The Blue Ridge range of the Appalachian Mountains lies in the extreme northwestern portion of South Carolina where the land surface elevation ranges from about 1,000 to 3,000 feet. Southeast of this region is located the Piedmont Plateau, which continues almost to the center of the State where it descends into the Coastal Plain (Landers, 1970). The State is divided into six climatological divisions based on topography, of which the highest is the Mountain Division located in the northwest corner of the State. The proposed Bad Creek Project is located in the Mountain Division on the southern edge of the Blue Ridge Escarpment. Portions of the lower reservoir and some alternative sites are located in the southern mountains climatological division of North Carolina, also a portion of the Blue Ridge range.
Climatological data for the project site as prepared by the Applicant are shown in Table 2-19. The climate of the project area is mild with lower temperatures than those experienced in the rest of South Carolina, due to higher elevation, latitude, and greater distance from the Atlantic shore. Mean annual solar radiation for the site area is 350 to 400 langleys per day, with a minimum of about 200 per day during the winter and a maximum of about 550 per day in the summer (U.S. Geological Survey, 1970). Average monthly temperatures range from about 40°F to 74°F over the annual cycle. The record low temperature for the area is -7°F while the record high is 99°F.
